headlines.article_text: UBS pretax profits jump 27% in third quarter to $3.59 billion Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points UBS reported a third-quarter pretax profit of nearly $3.6 billion, up 27% from a year earlier and broadly in line with forecasts. Performance was also boosted by strong inflows into its global wealth management business. With the integration of former rival Credit Suisse “firmly on track” for completion by year-end, CEO Sergio Ermotti said the Swiss banking giant remains committed to its global and regional footprint. In this article UBS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT This photograph shows a sign of Swiss giant banking UBS at a branch in Zurich on March 4, 2026. Fabrice Coffrini | AFP | Getty Images UBS reported a pretax profit of almost $3.6 billion in the third quarter, up 27% year over year, largely in line with consensus forecasts. The Swiss banking and asset management giant saw strong net inflows into its global wealth management business. Net profit was $2.7 billion for the third quarter, in line with estimates. UBS shares are up by around a quarter this year The Zurich-headquartered lender's common equity tier (CET) 1 capital ratio — a measure of a bank's solvency — reached 14.7% during the period, up from 14.4% the previous quarter. Strong inflows into its global wealth management business supported performance, with net new assets reaching $55.1 billion by the end of the quarter. UBS recorded $12.5 billion in client commitments across its wealth management and asset management businesses. In its third-quarter earnings statement Wednesday, the bank said the integration of Credit Suisse is "firmly on track" to be completed by year-end, delivering a total of $13.7 billion in cumulative cost savings, above earlier expectations of $13.5 billion. UBS battles with Swiss government over risk tools UBS remains locked in an ongoing wrangle with the Swiss government over proposals for increased capital buffers, aimed at insulating taxpayers from any future banking crisis and contagion from the bank's foreign subsidiaries following the Credit Suisse debacle. The bank is seen as systemically important to the Swiss economy. The country's upper house of parliament voted last month to require UBS to hold 90% of Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital, or about $16 billion in extra shares, as collateral to support its foreign subsidiaries. The level currently stands at around 45%. UBS wants it to be no more than 50%. Speaking with CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" Wednesday, Ermotti said the bank's clients expect it to be competitive. "90% would not, long-term, allow us to be a competitive player," Ermotti told CNBC's Carolin Roth. "I'm very concerned about this development." In an earlier statement, Ermotti said UBS' strong third-quarter performance underlines the benefits of its diversified global business model, adding that the lender remains "strategically committed to its diversified business model and its global and regional footprint." headlines.article_text: Robinhood shares fall as crypto slump weighs on profits Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Robinhood posted weaker-than-expected earnings for the third quarter and revenue that met Wall Street expectations. Transaction-based revenue saw a 19% gain year-over-year, driven by event contracts revenue, options and equities. Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55%. Investors are looking for signs that Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity. In this article HOOD Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Omar Marques | Lightrocket | Getty Images Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets. Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: 51 cents vs. 56 cents expected Revenue: $1.42 billion vs. $1.42 billion expected Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year. Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity. Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings. Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million. Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million. Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading. Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. headlines.article_text: Meta and Google-backed Jio Platforms’ shares soar over 21% on trading debut Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Jio raised 302 billion rupees ($3.2 billion) in the country's largest-ever IPO. Signage for Jio Platforms Ltd. ahead of the company's listing ceremony at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in Mumbai, India, on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. Bloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty Images Jio Platforms' shares rose 21.5% on their trading debut Wednesday after a record initial public offering that was lapped up by retail as well as institutional investors. Jio's market capitalization was 12.5 trillion rupees ($131 billion), making it the second most valued company in India after its parent Reliance Industries, as per NSE data. This paves the way for its eventual inclusion in key benchmark indices. That inclusion will generate sufficient demand and protect the share price from any oversupply, Deven Choksey, founder and managing director at wealth management firm DRChoksey FinServ, told CNBC. He added that some of the investors who acquired a stake in Jio around 2021 may want to exit in around six months, by which time the stock will likely be included in the MSCI index and the Nifty 50 . India's largest telecom and digital services player had offered 270 million shares in the IPO priced at 1,119 rupees apiece, raising 302 billion rupees ($3.2 billion) in the country's largest-ever IPO. The public issue was subscribed more than 22 times, with institutional investors leading the demand, according to data from the BSE. The qualified institutional portion was subscribed 70.55 times, while retail investors subscribed 2.72 times. The IPO was fully subscribed within 95 minutes of its opening on Oct. 21, Akash Ambani, managing director of Jio Platforms and heir of the Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani, said ahead of the listing. Global brokerage Nomura on Wednesday gave Jio Platforms a buy rating, setting a target price of 1,340 rupees, implying an upside of 19.7% to its IPO price. The brokerage said in a report that Jio's capex cycle is largely over and there is expected to be a sharp improvement in the company's free cash flow. Shares were last trading at 1,360 rupees. Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's flagship company, Reliance Industries , owns more than a 66% stake in Jio Platforms, followed by Meta Platforms ' affiliate Jaadhu Holdings that owns nearly 10% and Google International, which owns 7.7%, as per LSEG data. Leading global funds such as BlackRock, Capital Group and GIC participated in Jio's anchor book portion of the total fundraise, which is set aside for large institutional investors before the IPO opens for public bidding.
